rationale: Dense colored grain is plainly visible across the sky, building walls, shadows, and hillside. Major shapes and edges remain clear, while the pervasive noise interferes with surface textures and fine detail.

Bicycle lettering, frames, spokes, and background architecture are clearly resolved. Exposure preserves useful detail in the bright scene, colors are plausible, and no material compression or processing artifacts are apparent.

Pervasive colored grain and softness reduce detail, while glass reflections overlap the firearms and weaken their local contrast. The firearms remain recognizable, but the small exhibit labels are difficult to resolve, supporting the limited-detail caveat.

The leaf veins and droplets are distinctly resolved, and the insect's body, legs, and antennae remain visible. Exposure retains the leaf's texture. The dark background is smooth and defocused with modest grain; small differences in perceived sharpness do not materially contradict the explanation.

A large saturated reflection obscures the middle of the box and part of its title. Remaining lettering is readable and the coins are recognizable, though their fine markings are soft. General softness and modest grain are visible.

The thermometer is recognizable, but its logo and casing edges are visibly soft. Its dark digital display extends beyond the bottom image boundary, leaving some digits cut off. These observations support the explanation and limited-detail caveat.

Hair, facial features, and molded clothing textures are clearly visible, particularly on the left figure. The right figure is somewhat softer, as acknowledged. Bright highlights preserve substantial surface detail, colors are plausible, and the background is smooth.

Writing on the central orange and left green notes is clearly legible with strong contrast. Slight grain and softness are visible, especially on peripheral notes and the dark background, without materially obscuring the main text.
